images.seen: A man wrestling the patio umbrella closed as a black storm front swallows the last of the sunshine, leaves flying across the tiles. Thursday.
lines: The umbrella is coming down in the storm's final two minutes of notice.
Half the sky is still summer; the other half is why he is hurrying.
Leaves already sideways: the storm sent its calling card ahead.

images.seen: A young man in a parked car filming a lightning bolt through the rain-beaded windscreen, wet suburban street beyond. Sunday.
lines: The car is the best hide this country makes for lightning season.
Rain on the glass, bolt in the frame, and not one drop on the photographer.
Front-row seats, full cover, wipers off: storm-watching done properly.

images.seen: A night storm over a suburban street — rain slanting through the streetlight, lightning glowing behind the clouds, one big bare tree over the walls. Tuesday.
lines: The rain is coming through the streetlight at forty-five degrees, which means wind joined in.
Lightning behind the cloud: the storm is working with the lights off.
That old tree has stood through a hundred of these and is counting this one too.

images.seen: Lightning splitting a purple night sky over a double garage, the gutter overflowing in a stream past the hosepipe, jacaranda petals on the wet paving. Monday.
lines: The gutter gave up on the downpipe and started its own waterfall.
Purple sky, purple petals: the storm colour-matched the driveway tonight.
The overflow says the roof got a month of rain in one evening.
